title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Platinum (Pt, Z=78) is 195.084(9)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Platinum (Pt, Z=78) as 195.084(9), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 78, symbol Pt, as Platinum. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Platinum as 195.084(9). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: Pt-190 relative atomic mass 189.9599297(63), isotopic composition 0.00012(2); Pt-192 relative atomic mass 191.9610387(32), isotopic composition 0.00782(24); Pt-194 relative atomic mass 193.9626809(10), isotopic composition 0.3286(40); Pt-195 relative atomic mass 194.9647917(10), isotopic composition 0.3378(24); Pt-196 relative atomic mass 195.96495209(99), isotopic composition 0.2521(34); Pt-198 relative atomic mass 197.9678949(23), isotopic composition 0.07356(130). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
